mainEntity.name: Is a CD or a high-yield savings account better?

acceptedAnswer.text: A CD usually wins if you won't need the money before it matures and rates fall or stay flat. A high-yield savings account wins if you may need the money, or if rates rise during the term. Many savers use both.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I withdraw from a CD early?

acceptedAnswer.text: You pay an early withdrawal penalty, commonly a set number of days or months of interest. If you break the CD early enough, the penalty can exceed the interest earned and reduce your principal.

mainEntity.name: Do high-yield savings account rates change?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. HYSA rates are variable and banks can change them at any time, typically following moves in the Federal Reserve's policy rate.

mainEntity.name: Are CDs and high-yield savings accounts insured?

acceptedAnswer.text: At FDIC-insured banks, both are covered up to $250,000 per depositor, per bank, per ownership category. Credit union accounts have equivalent NCUA coverage.
